findings.title: Raw HTML from remote/feed stored and rendered unsanitized (stored XSS)
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import stores the HTML it fetches as the post body with cook_method raw_html, so Post#cook returns it as-is. That HTML comes from Readability output or RSS item content. The feed path in particular unescapes HTML entities and keeps every tag, including script. Nothing sanitizes it before it is rendered on the forum and in the embed view via `raw post.cooked`. Anyone who controls the feed or the remote page can inject script into the Discourse origin.

findings.title: URL interpolated unescaped into HTML attribute
findings.body: The imported_from footer builds `#{url}` without escaping. A URL containing a quote or angle bracket can inject markup or script. Because the post is rendered as raw HTML, this is exploitable.

findings.title: Mutates caller's string; SHA computed before absolutize
findings.body: `contents <<` modifies the caller's string in place, and it raises on a frozen string. The SHA1 is computed on the content before URLs are absolutized; that part is fine, but repeated calls with the same string object keep appending the footer, so the hash changes on every call and the post is revised again each time.

findings.title: Port check ignores scheme
findings.body: The prefix omits the port whenever it is 80 or 443, regardless of scheme. For example, `https://host:80` would wrongly drop the explicit port and produce incorrect absolute URLs.

findings.title: Referer injected into inline script
findings.body: `request.referer` is interpolated into a JavaScript string literal with only HTML escaping, which does not escape for a JS context. The referer is attacker-influenced, and its host is checked only loosely. Using it as the postMessage target origin is also fragile. It should be JS-escaped (j/escape_javascript) or derived from the embeddable_host setting.

findings.title: Unauthenticated requests enqueue jobs that fetch arbitrary URLs
findings.body: Every cache miss enqueues a retrieve job carrying an arbitrary embed_url. The host check only happens later, in the job, against an exact host match. Throttling is per URL, so varying the query string bypasses it and lets anyone flood Sidekiq with jobs.

findings.title: Start-discussion branch unreachable
findings.body: The topic's first post always exists, so the 'start_discussion' branch never renders. It is also suspect that `end if` is used here; it is valid Ruby but confusing.

findings.title: open-uri resource leak and per-item failures abort the whole poll
findings.body: `open(url)` is never closed. If one item has nil content, `scrub` raises NoMethodError and the rest of the feed is skipped. The job also has retry disabled. In addition, `feed_key` is never used.

findings.title: Polling entire feed synchronously per retrieval
findings.body: Each topic retrieval re-polls and re-imports the entire feed inline. This happens for every distinct embed URL that is not yet known, which causes heavy repeated work.

findings.title: Spec expects TopicRetriever but controller enqueues job
findings.body: The controller calls Jobs.enqueue rather than TopicRetriever.new directly. The test passes only because jobs run inline when queue_jobs is false in the test environment, which makes it brittle. It also never asserts the 'loading' render.

findings.title: Revision not saved when import updates a raw_html post
findings.body: Post#save's before_save re-cooks the post. For raw_html posts the content changes only as raw, but the PostRevisor return value and save result are ignored in TopicEmbed. A failed save is silent, yet content_sha1 is still updated, so later changes are never retried.
